fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Open Lawn Area; Access Drive; Detached Structure; Dense Vegetation
fr.considerations: Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with tall, reflective posts on both sides to define the opening, especially in low-light or smoky conditions.
• Trim trees and shrubs along both sides of the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Maintain a vertical clearance of at least 14 feet along the entire driveway length to allow fire and rescue vehicles to pass through.
• Create or designate a turnaround area near the main residence so emergency vehicles do not have to back out the full length of the driveway.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the sides of the driveway to reduce the risk of fire reaching vehicles or blocking responder movement.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of parked vehicles, debris, and movable obstacles at all times.
• Post clear directional signage at any driveway forks or decision points so responders can navigate directly to the main residence and detached structures without delay.
• Label both the main residence and each detached structure with visible unit or building markers so responders can distinguish between them on arrival.
• If a gate exists at the driveway entrance, install a Knox Box or provide emergency responders with a key or access code so they are not delayed at entry.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Open Green Space; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route; Vegetation Along Driveway; Scattered Trees; Mixed Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back shrubs and low-growing plants that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house on all sides.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure so individual trees are more separated from each other and from the house.
• Remove low-hanging branches on large trees close to the house, cutting them up from the ground to reduce the path fire can take into the tree canopy.
• Clear dead leaves, fallen branches, and other dry plant material that has collected against the house foundation and along exterior walls.
• Separate shrubs and smaller plants growing beneath the large trees nearest the structure so fire cannot move easily from the ground up into the tree tops.
• Keep the single driveway clear of overhanging branches from the vegetation growing along its edges so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway back far enough that a fire truck can move through without contact with plants.
• Thin scattered trees in the open areas between the tree clusters to break up the connected vegetation around the property.
• Remove any shrubs or small trees that are growing directly against or beneath the eaves of the structure.
• Keep the open green space adjacent to the property mowed or cut short to reduce the amount of dry plant material that could carry fire toward the house.
• Move any wood piles, lumber, or stored combustible materials away from the exterior walls
